body.content:
To reduce no-shows, remind clients before every visit, set a no-show policy they see before they book, and take a deposit for long or costly services. Below are 9 tactics small salons, clinics and studios use, with what each one takes to set up.

Why clients miss appointments: the common reasons

Most missed visits are not rudeness. The same few causes come up again and again: the client forgot, the booking was made weeks ago, something came up and cancelling felt awkward, or nothing was at stake. Each tactic below answers one of them.

What no-shows cost a small business

A missed visit costs the price of the service and the slot you could have sold to someone else. Multiply your average booking value by the visits missed each month: at [your average booking value] and [your missed visits a month], that is the amount these tactics are trying to win back.

1. Send appointment reminder texts

Reminders are the cheapest fix on this list. Most clients who miss a visit simply forgot, and a message the day before brings the booking back to mind. If you want to reduce no-shows with one change this week, start here.

Our automatic reminders go out by text and email, and you choose the timing.

Text or email?

Text reminders get read within minutes, while email often sits unopened. Send text reminders for next-day visits and keep email for bookings made weeks ahead. Clients can reply to text reminders to confirm or cancel.

2. Take deposits

Ask for a deposit when the client books, and say in plain words when it is kept (our guide to writing a deposit policy has sample wording). A deposit is the strongest way to reduce no-shows for long or expensive services, because the client has something to lose.

3. Keep a waitlist

A waitlist will not reduce no-shows on its own, but it fills the gap when one happens. When a slot opens, the next person on the list gets a text and can claim it.

4. Let clients reschedule online

Many no-shows are people who could not face a phone call to move their booking. A reschedule link in every reminder lets them pick a new time in a few taps, which helps reduce no-shows without extra work at the front desk.

5. Confirm by text

Ask clients to reply YES to confirm. Anyone who has not replied by the evening before gets a call. Confirmation requests work because they turn a passive booking into a small promise.

6. Overbook carefully

If a slot type is missed often, book one extra client into it. Overbooking only softens the cost of a missed visit, so use it for short services where a double booking can be absorbed.

7. Follow up with repeat no-shows

A client who misses twice gets a friendly message and a request to pay a deposit next time. Most businesses that track this find a few clients cause most of the missed visits, and handling them directly is the fastest win.

8. Thank clients who show up

A short thank-you after each visit, with a link to book again, keeps the relationship warm. Clients who feel noticed are less likely to skip.

9. Make cancelling easy

A client who can cancel in one tap will cancel instead of disappearing. Put a cancel link in every reminder and accept cancellations up to the last hour.

Set a no-show policy and what to charge (salon and clinic example)

A no-show policy tells clients, before they book, what happens if they miss a visit: whether the deposit is kept, whether a fee applies, and how late they can cancel without a charge. Most guides treat it as part of your cancellation policy, so keep both on one page and show it in the booking confirmation and every reminder. A salon might charge [your fee] for a missed colour appointment and nothing for a cancellation made [your notice period] ahead. Our cancellation policy template has wording you can copy.

What is a good no-show rate, and how to work out yours

Your no-show rate is the number of missed visits divided by all booked visits in a period. Work it out every month from your booking history, before and after each change, so you can see which tactic moved it. What counts as good depends on the kind of business, so compare your no-show rate with your own past months first: [your no-show rate last month].

Wrap-up

No single tactic gets missed visits to zero. Start with appointment reminders and deposits, then add the rest as your calendar fills. Our plans include reminders on every tier.
